findings.selection_note: Three findings selected for patching: the two high-signal issues with failing tests (F-SEC-002-COV-002, F-COV-001) and the high-severity security finding with no test (F-SEC-001). Remaining findings are low-priority coverage gaps documented but not patched in this run.

accepted_findings.description: find() missing bounds check — negative indices alias silently, out-of-range raises IndexError not ValueError
accepted_findings.verifier_reasoning: Diff adds 0 <= x < len(self.parent) guard and raises ValueError for both cases. Both previously-failing tests now pass. Recursive path-compression call is protected by same guard since parent[] only contains valid indices.

accepted_findings.description: put() evicts head.next (MRU) instead of tail.prev (LRU) — wrong eviction order
accepted_findings.verifier_reasoning: Diff correctly changes evict = self.head.next to evict = self.tail.prev. test_eviction_removes_least_recently_used was FAILED, now PASSED. No regressions. Fix aligns with LRU semantics: _add_front() inserts at head, so tail.prev is always the LRU node.

accepted_findings.description: compute_key() calls eval() on caller-supplied input — arbitrary code execution
accepted_findings.verifier_reasoning: eval(expression) eliminated entirely. Replaced with unconditional TypeError. No eval/exec calls remain in codebase. No existing test calls compute_key() — method is dead code. For a security finding, removing the vulnerable code path is the correct tradeoff over wrapping it. No regressions.
accepted_findings.tests_before: 7/10 passed (3 unrelated failures from other bugs)

manual_review_estimate.note: 15 min per finding for a senior engineer: read context, understand the fix, validate test output, check edge cases
